capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Osnabrück'; the bishops resided at Iburg Castle from c. 1100 until the palace in the town was completed in 1673.

correction.text: the Hochstift Osnabrück round Osnabrück, a stand-in circle

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Osnabrück row). The page gives no area ('Area and population: not given'), no boundary and none of the district names (Vörden, Fürstenau, Wiedenbrück, Reckenberg); a 30 km circle at Osnabrück (about 2,800 km2), soft. In 1236 'the Count of Tecklenburg was forced to renounce all jurisdiction over the town of Osnabrück', which is jurisdiction, not land.

ledger.note: 1225: the ecclesiastical principality. 'An ecclesiastical principality of the Holy Roman Empire from 1225 until 1803'; infobox 'Created on collapse of Saxony: 1225'. The diocese itself was erected in 772.

1648: the alternation. The Treaty of Osnabrück restored the religious status of 1624: 'Henceforth, the prince-bishops would alternate between Catholic and Protestant officeholders', the Protestants 'from the cadets of the House of Brunswick-Lüneburg'. Same state, new regime.

1803: 'The bishopric was dissolved in the German Mediatisation of 1803, when it was incorporated into the neighboring' Electorate of Hanover (infobox 'secularised to Hanover'). The last prince-bishop was Prince Frederick (1764-1803).

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary or area; the circle is a stand-in.

SHAPE. A 30 km circle at Osnabrück (8.05E 52.28N); the gazetteer has the place 'Osnabrück'. The page names no district and no acquisition.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Area, boundary and acquisitions (Vörden, Fürstenau, Wiedenbrück, Reckenberg, Bramsche, Quakenbrück and Melle are not on the page). (2) The 1236 Tecklenburg renunciation concerns jurisdiction over the town. (3) The 1802 Hanoverian occupation is not on the page.
